title: Computational Constancy Measures of Texts—Yule’s K and Rényi’s Entropy
summary: The paper relates Yule’s K to an approximation of second-order Rényi entropy and compares constancy measures across natural texts and program code. Its exploratory comparison places the Voynich parts near an Arabic text by word-level measures, but says the observation provides only limited evidence and requires further study.
established: The authors mathematically relate Yule’s K to an approximation of second-order Rényi entropy and find rapid, stable convergence of approximate higher-order entropy in the corpora examined; they report that K does not identify authors reliably (abstract and conclusion).

For the Voynich comparison they split the transliteration by Currier A and B and define words by spaces. Table 1 gives 7,460 and 18,495 word tokens respectively, so the A word point in Figure 5 is plotted at its full available size, below the 10,000-token reference used for most comparisons.

The word-level points for both manuscript parts fall near the Arabic book in the Figure 5 comparison of distinct types and approximate second-order entropy; the authors note that punctuation counted as characters inflates the comparison alphabets and treat their language and abjad interpretation as tentative (section 4.3).

open.question: How distinctive are the observed second-order entropy and vocabulary-size positions when compared with layout-matched nonlinguistic generators and independently sampled historical texts?
open.check: Fix tokenization, sample sizes and the entropy calculation on public material, then compare held-out manuscript pages with matched samples and multiple generator seeds.
